key_insight: AI rewriting can make radiology text look cleaner while worsening alignment with the underlying image, creating a “slop paradox” where standardization and teaching-case rewrites are more harmful to multimodal fidelity than EHR summarization.
clinical_relevance: For AI-assisted radiology documentation and multimodal dataset building, text cleanup should be evaluated not just for readability, but for whether it preserves uncertainty and image-text meaning.
method: 450 chest X-ray reports from the Indiana University dataset
Generated three synthetic rewrite types: EHR summarization, standardized rewriting, and teaching-case preparation
Measured entity loss, hedging loss, and BiomedCLIP image-text similarity change
evidence_signal: EHR summarization erased 51.4% of clinical entities and 43.7% of hedging language, but image-text alignment dropped only 2.5%; standardized and teaching-case rewrites preserved more entities yet reduced alignment by 14.9–16.5%.
watch_item: Rare pathology monitoring may miss degradation because no rare-vs-common difference survived correction, so task type appears more important than diagnosis-specific safeguards.
paper_title: The Slop Paradox: How Synthetic Standardization Erodes Clinical Uncertainty and Cross-Modal Alignment in AI-Rewritten Radiology Reports
